Variables.CDISC Notes: This variable is used to explain why the record is not included in the PK NCA.

Variables.Variable Label: Reason for PK NCA Exclusion of w (N)

Numeric representation of the COHORT variable. There must be a one-to-one mapping between COHORT and COHORTN. When COHORT and COHORTN are present, then, on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

Units associated with TRTRINT

Variables.Variable Label: Percent Diff. Nominal vs. Actual Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: Derived variable using a standard percent difference formula: (100*(DOSEA-DOSEP)/(DOSEP)). DOSPCTDF is required if both DOSEA and DOSEP are populated.
Usually expressed as the number of repeated administrations of DOSE within a specific time period for multiple dose studies.

This is a record-level identifier that reflects cycle and may be of particular importance for studies that examine concentrations in cancer patients. There must be a one-to-one mapping between ACYCLE and ACYCLEC. When ACYCLE and ACYCLEC are present, then, on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

Character representation of the ACYCLE variable. Text characterizing to which analysis cycle the record belongs. This is a record-level identifier that reflects cycle and may be of particular importance for studies that examine concentrations in cancer patients. There must be a one-to-one mapping between ACYCLE and ACYCLEC. When ACYCLE and ACYCLEC are present, then, on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

Variables.Variable Label: First Date of Dose for Analyte
Variables.CDISC Notes: Date of first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE for a subject in a study where multiple doses have been given. Note that FANLDT may not match TRTSDT or any of TRxxSDT values.

Variables.Variable Label: First Time of Dose for Analyte
Variables.CDISC Notes: Time of first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE for a subject in a study where multiple doses have been given. If treatment is given over a duration multiple times, this variable will reflect the start time of the first dose.

Variables.Variable Label: First Datetime of Dose for Analyte
Variables.CDISC Notes: Date and time of first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE for a subject in a study where multiple doses have been given. If treatment is given over a duration multiple times, this variable will reflect the start date and time of the first dose.

Variables.Variable Label: First End Date of Dose for Analyte
Variables.CDISC Notes: End date of first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE for a subject in a study where multiple doses have been given. Note that FANLEDT may not match TRTEDT or any of TRxxEDT values.

Variables.Variable Label: First End Time of Dose for Analyte
Variables.CDISC Notes: End time of first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE for a subject in a study where multiple doses have been given. If treatment is given over a duration multiple times, this variable will reflect the end time of the first dose.

Variables.Variable Label: First End Datetime of Dose for Analyte
Variables.CDISC Notes: End date and time of first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE for a subject in a study where multiple doses have been given. If treatment is given over a duration multiple times, this variable will reflect the end date and time of the first dose.

Variables.Variable Label: Reference Date of Dose for Analyte
Variables.CDISC Notes: Date of reference exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. Based on PC.PCRFTDTC and related to the analyzed profile. If this is a treatment over time, then this is typically the start of the dosing duration.

Variables.Variable Label: Reference Time of Dose for Analyte
Variables.CDISC Notes: Time of reference exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. Based on PC.PCRFTDTC and related to the analyzed profile. If this is a treatment over time, then this is typically the start of the dosing duration.

Variables.Variable Label: Reference Datetime of Dose for Analyte
Variables.CDISC Notes: Date and time of reference exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. Based on PC.PCRFTDTC and related to the analyzed profile. If this is a treatment over time, then this is typically the start of the dosing duration.

Variables.Variable Label: Reference End Date of Dose for Analyte
Variables.CDISC Notes: The end date of reference exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. Must be related to the time recorded in PC.PCRFTDTC and to the analyzed profile. If dosing occurs over an interval, this should be populated. If populated, ADOSEDUR and DOSEDURU are required to be filled out.

Variables.Variable Label: Reference End Time of Dose for Analyte
Variables.CDISC Notes: The end time of the reference exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. Must be related to the time recorded in PC.PCRFTDTC and to the analyzed profile. If dosing occurs over an interval, this should be populated. If populated, ADOSEDUR and DOSEDURU are required to be filled out.

Variables.Variable Label: Ref. End Datetime of Dose for Analyte
Variables.CDISC Notes: The end date and time of the reference exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. Must be related to the time recorded in PC.PCRFTDTC and to the analyzed profile. If dosing occurs over an interval, this should be populated. If populated, ADOSEDUR and DOSEDURU are required to be filled out.

Variables.Variable Label: Nom. Rel. Time from Analyte First Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: This is the planned elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. For studies with an extended duration infusion, use the define to document if this is from the start or end of the infusion.

Variables.Variable Label: Act. Rel. Time from Analyte First Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: This is the actual elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. Note that this is referring to the first dose available for a particular drug. It is useful in multiple-dosing situations.

Variables.Variable Label: Nom. Rel. End Time from First Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: This is the planned elapsed end time of sampling interval from first exposure to study treatment.

Variables.Variable Label: Act. Rel. End Time from First Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: This is the actual elapsed end time of sampling interval from first exposure to study treatment.

Variables.Variable Label: Rel. Time from First Dose Unit
Variables.CDISC Notes: This is the unit for all elapsed times from first dose.

Variables.Variable Label: Nominal Rel. Time from Ref. Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: This is the planned elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from reference exposure to study treatment.

Variables.Variable Label: Actual Rel. Time from Ref. Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: This is the actual elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from reference exposure to study treatment.

Variables.Variable Label: Modified Rel. Time from Ref. Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: This variable could be used to modify the ARRLT variable based on analysis needs (e.g., setting negative values to zero or having a mix of nominal and actual time based of TMPCTDF).

Variables.Variable Label: Nominal Rel. End Time from Ref. Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: This is the planned elapsed end time of sampling interval from reference exposure to study treatment.

Variables.Variable Label: Actual Rel. End Time from Ref. Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: This is the actual elapsed end time of sampling interval from reference exposure to study treatment.

Variables.Variable Label: Modified Rel. End Time from Ref. Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: This variable could be used to modify the AERRLT variable based on analysis needs (e.g., setting negative values to zero or having a mix of nominal and actual time based on TMPCTDF).

Variables.Variable Label: Rel. Time from Ref. Dose Unit
Variables.CDISC Notes: This is the unit for all elapsed times from reference dose.

Variables.Variable Label: Percent Diff. Nominal vs. Actual Time
Variables.CDISC Notes: This is the percent difference between nominal and actual time. It is derived by using the standard percent difference formula: 100*( NRRLT - ARRLT)/( NRRLT).

Variables.CDISC Notes: The analysis visit description; required if an analysis is done by nominal, assigned or analysis visit. AVISIT may contain the visit names as observed (i.e., from SDTM VISIT), derived visit names, time window names, conceptual descriptions (such as Average, Endpoint, etc.), or a combination of any of these. AVISIT is a derived field and does not have to map to VISIT from the SDTM. AVISIT represents the analysis visit of the record, but it does not mean that the record was analyzed. There are often multiple records for the same subject and parameter that have the same value of AVISIT. ANLzzFL and other variables may be needed to identify the records selected for any given analysis. See ADaMIG v1.2, Section 3.3.8, for information about flag variables. AVISIT should be unique for a given analysis visit window. In the event a record does not fall within any predefined analysis time-point window, AVISIT can be populated in any way that the producer chooses to indicate this fact (i.e., blank or "Not Windowed"). The way that AVISIT is calculated, including the variables used in its derivation, should be indicated in the variable metadata for AVISIT. The values and the rules for deriving AVISIT may be different for different parameters within the same dataset. Values of AVISIT are producer-defined and are often directly usable in clinical study report (CSR) displays.

Data Structures.CDISC Notes: One record per subject per parameter per analysis visit per analysis timepoint
